channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading in record $81.3B IPO
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic’s Class A shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the $83 IPO price, in the largest public offering on record. The debut makes the Claude maker the first frontier AI lab on the public markets — and sets the benchmark every other lab will now be judged against.

item.title: Build your own browser agent with Gemini Computer Use: the complete hands-on tutorial
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google's Computer Use tool went GA on October 30: Gemini sees your screen and returns clicks, keystrokes, and scrolls, and your code runs them. This tutorial builds a working browser agent with the Interactions API and Playwright — the full loop, the safety gates, and the pricing — with every call verified against Google's docs.

item.title: A 1:1 Minecraft replica of Earth went viral — but the 'entire world' claim is doing heavy lifting
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 36-second flyover of blocky San Francisco and New York racked up 20 million views on X and hundreds of upvotes on Reddit within hours. The builder says he trained a 'world-to-Minecraft generator' on maps data — but the thread underneath is doing what Reddit does best: checking the fine print.

item.title: Gemini can now drive your Mac: Google’s computer-use agent clicks, types and files for you
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google is rolling out computer use in the Gemini app for Mac, letting the assistant click through menus, fill in forms and finish multi-step jobs in a background window while you keep working. The catch: it needs the deepest permissions macOS offers, and Google warns it can delete files or share them by mistake.

item.title: QMD: turn your notes and docs into a local hybrid search engine your coding agent can query
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: QMD 2.9.0 is a local search engine for your markdown: BM25, vector search, LLM reranking and query expansion, all on your machine with no API key — plus an MCP server your agent can call. This tutorial installs it, indexes a real docs folder, and measures every search mode.

item.title: Satya Nadella: every Microsoft employee will one day be a 'manager of agents'
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: At the DealBook Summit, Microsoft's CEO explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 employees — and sketched a future where directing AI agents, not doing the work directly, is the job.

item.title: A 3-minute animated film about AI and the craft of programming has Reddit in a philosophical spiral
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A painterly short film starring a weary programmer and a very calm praying mantis hit r/ChatGPT this morning — and the thread underneath it turned into one of the most honest debates about AI, craft and livelihoods the site has had in a while.

item.title: Coral hands-on: give your coding agent a gateway that writes its own tools
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Coral 1.10.0 is a self-hosted MCP gateway where agents write short TypeScript programs that call your providers — each one sandboxed, policy-checked, and saveable as a reusable tool. This tutorial installs it, wires up a local ticket API with no tokens, and ends with a custom tool your agent can call by name.

item.title: California proposes emergency shutdown power for frontier AI models — and state-licensed auditors inside every lab
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Governor Gavin Newsom’s new report, “AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond,” would let California order a frontier model shut down in an emergency, put every large developer under continuous oversight by state-licensed auditors, and give the state standby power to cap AI that designs its own successors.

item.title: Run AI in the browser: build a private semantic search app with Transformers.js
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Transformers.js 4.3.2 runs real embedding models in the browser — no server, no API key. This tutorial builds a private semantic search app with it, measures every step, and shows the one query that gets the wrong answer and why.

item.title: Cloudflare open-sources Clairic: its document-extraction models are now free to run anywhere
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Cloudflare has released open weights for Clairic and its new 9-billion-parameter sibling Clairic-flash, a month after the extraction model’s hosted-only preview. Both turn receipts, PDFs, and support tickets into typed data — and developers can now download and run them on their own hardware.

item.title: Reverse-engineer any company’s marketing machine: hands-on with REM
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: REM turns one link into an evidence-cited teardown of how a company gets customers — paid ads, pixels, SEO, founders, funnel. This tutorial installs it from source, runs the no-key teardown on Linear, and wires it into your agent over MCP.

item.title: OpenAI’s models rewrote AMD’s GPU circuits — and found a year’s worth of design gains in under five months
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI says its models rewrote the circuits in AMD’s flagship GPU design for up to 14% better power, performance and area — and some of those changes are already in a design AMD sent for manufacturing.

item.title: OpenAI says its coding agents now finish 46% of two-to-four-hour research tasks on their own
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI’s second report on AI-assisted research finds its coding agents completing nearly half of multi-hour research tasks with no human stepping in — but the gains are jagged, and the hardest engineering work still belongs to people.

item.title: Give your AI agent the live web: search, scrape, and crawl with Firecrawl — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Firecrawl is the sixth most-trending repo on GitHub today: one API that gives your agent live search, scraping, crawling, and an agent endpoint. This tutorial runs every endpoint on the free tier — 1,000 credits a month, no card — and builds a local Markdown mirror of a docs site.

item.title: Citi and PNC rewrite their terms: give an AI agent your bank login and the risk is yours
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Citibank updated its Online User Agreement this week to say customers who hand their bank login to a third-party AI agent own whatever happens next — even if the agent is hacked. PNC, Citizens and Wells Fargo are moving the same way.

item.title: He replaced Notion, Maps and his file manager with one app Claude rewrites on request — meet Equin
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: After seven months and more than 8,000 Claude sessions, one developer rebuilt every app he uses daily inside a single open-source platform — and when an app is missing a feature, he just asks it to add one. A 1:55 video on r/ClaudeAI shows the “self-evolving personal OS” in action.

item.title: Build an agent that remembers you: hands-on with Letta's Agent SDK
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Most agents start from zero every session. Letta's Agent SDK builds stateful agents whose memory persists across conversations — create one, correct a fact it holds about you, and watch it rewrite its own memory, then resume it from a fresh process and see it remember.

item.title: Federal investigators bypassed the safeguards on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok — and got viable attack plans in under 12 hours
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The Government Accountability Office went undercover on the four most-used AI chatbots in spring 2026. Every safeguard fired first — and every one was bypassed. Each platform produced a viable attack plan in under 12 hours.

item.title: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq today as ANT after pricing the largest IPO in history at $83 a share
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion — the largest stock-market debut on record — and its shares start trading on Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT.

item.title: Strip the noise, keep the voice: hands-on with Inworld's Voice Isolator and SAVA
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Inworld open-sourced the voice-isolation and turn-taking models behind its realtime voice products. I installed both, ran them on the repo's own noisy sample, and measured it: silent gaps cut by ~50 dB, speech kept within a decibel, and a realtime twin that matches the offline model to 0.999 correlation.

item.title: See what your AI agent actually did: hands-on with Arize Phoenix observability
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Three frontier agent models shipped in 48 hours. The question isn't whether you can build an agent — it's whether you can see what it did. This tutorial wires a local agent to Arize Phoenix, traces every call, and turns the results into evals and experiments — no API key, no cloud, no cost.

item.title: Inworld open-sources a voice isolator that pulls clean speech out of noisy recordings — live, in 20 milliseconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Inworld’s Voice Isolator v1 is a small, Apache-2.0 open-weight model that strips crowd noise, music and room echo from speech — and a realtime twin does it live with 20 milliseconds of look-ahead. A 39-second demo on r/LocalLLaMA shows the before-and-after.

item.title: Red-team your own chatbot: hands-on with Microsoft's PyRIT
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft's AI red team open-sourced the toolkit it uses to break chatbots. Install PyRIT, point it at a local model, and run a real jailbreak scan — no API keys, no GPU, no cloud.

item.title: California pulls Waymo off its freeways — and Waymo pulls itself off every US highway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: California’s DMV barred Waymo’s driverless cars from state freeways after repeated construction-zone incursions, calling the service an ‘imminent hazard’ to public safety. Waymo has now paused freeway rides nationwide.
